issues.legal_issue: An owner who has no control over independently operated factory businesses is not an occupier liable for licensing failures merely because the premises and machinery were made available to those businesses.
material_facts: The owner had closed his factory and did not join the five partnerships formed by former workers.
Under leave-and-licence agreements, the partnerships used the premises and machinery in return for fixed payments and operated their manufacturing businesses independently.
The owner had no control over the partnerships, and the machinery had been specifically entrusted to their custody or use.
The State issued a notification applying the Factories Act to the premises, and the owner was prosecuted for failing to obtain factory licences.
issues.conclusion: The owner was not an occupier under section 2(n) or section 85(1)(ii) in these circumstances and could not be held liable for failing to obtain the licences; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(n) defines an occupier as the person having ultimate control over a factory’s affairs. Under section 85(1)(ii), a notification applying the Act to a place where workers are not employed by its owner requires that the workers work with the owner’s permission or under an agreement with the owner. A genuine arrangement transferring the premises and machinery to independent businesses, without the owner’s control or the required connection with the workers, does not meet that condition. Rule 3A requires an occupier to obtain a licence. Section 93(3)(ii) also indicates that an owner’s responsibility for fencing machinery belonging to the owner arises where it has not been specifically entrusted to an occupier. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.factory_licensing_prosecution: A person was prosecuted for failing to obtain a licence required for a factory.
predicates.premises_covered_by_extension_notice: The premises were made subject to a notice applying factory regulation to them.
predicates.workers_not_employed_by_owner: The people working at the premises were not employed by the owner.
predicates.workers_had_owner_permission: The workers carried on their work with the owner’s permission.
predicates.workers_worked_under_owner_agreement: The workers carried on their work under an agreement with the owner.
predicates.workers_operated_independent_businesses: The workers formed and operated businesses independently of the owner.
predicates.owner_lacked_ultimate_control: The owner did not have ultimate control over the affairs of the businesses operating at the premises.

issues.definition: When a factory-licensing prosecution concerns premises covered by an extension notice, workers who are not employed by the owner, lack the required permission or agreement, and operate independently without the owner’s ultimate control do not make the owner an occupier liable for the licensing failure.

issues.legal_issue: An owner is not liable for a machinery-fencing duty applicable to machinery belonging to the owner when that machinery has been specifically entrusted to an occupier’s custody or use.
material_facts: The owner made the factory machinery available to the five partnerships under leave-and-licence agreements.
The machinery and plant had been specifically entrusted to the partnerships’ custody or use.
The prosecution concerned the owner’s alleged failure to obtain factory licences; the Court considered the machinery-fencing provision in addressing the owner’s asserted statutory responsibility.
issues.conclusion: The owner could not be made liable under section 93(3)(ii) in respect of machinery specifically entrusted to the partnerships.
issues.legal_principle: Section 93(3)(ii) makes an owner responsible for fencing machinery and plant belonging to the owner when it has not been specifically entrusted to an occupier’s custody or use. The Court treated that provision as showing that the owner’s responsibility turns on whether the machinery was entrusted to the occupier. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.factory_owner_duty_liability_case: A proceeding concerns an owner’s liability for a duty relating to machinery at a factory.
predicates.machinery_belonged_to_owner: The machinery at issue belonged to the owner of the premises.
predicates.machinery_specifically_entrusted_to_occu: The owner specifically entrusted the machinery to an occupier’s custody or use.

issues.definition: In a proceeding about an owner’s machinery-related factory duty, the owner is not liable for the duty that applies to machinery left unentrusted when the owner specifically entrusted the machinery to an occupier.
